title: Blanket fasting instructions can be read as postponing all insulin
clause: Supplied 5.1, 8.1(vi), Explanation I; clinical safety review, not a verified statutory offence.
assessment: JUDGEMENT — materially unsafe ambiguity, CONFIRMED LIVE in page text; no evidence of patient injury.
quoted_text: "If you take diabetes medicines or insulin, bring them and take them after the fasting sample, with your meal." The check-up page similarly says "bring diabetes medicines with you to take after the blood sample."
why_it_breaches: A general instruction to defer insulin/diabetes medicines can mislead patients whose basal insulin must continue or whose fasting regimen requires individual adjustment, undermining genuinely safe educational communication.
compliant_alternative: Replace both preparation paragraphs with: "Fast only if your doctor or laboratory has confirmed that your particular test requires it, and follow the duration they give you. Water is usually allowed. If you use insulin or other diabetes medicines, obtain an individual plan for fasting, dose timing and meals before the test. Do not omit or delay insulin, especially basal insulin, or change medicines solely because of this website. If you develop symptoms of low blood sugar, treat them promptly and contact your care team; do not continue fasting just to complete a test. Bring your medicine list and previous reports." Have Dr. Ajay approve the wording and align staff instructions with it.
seo_aeo_note: Preserve preparation FAQs and test names; qualified instructions remain useful in answer engines without giving a one-size-fits-all medication order.
client_input_needed: Dr. Ajay's approved fasting/insulin protocol and clinical sign-off for both pages.

title: Diagnostic descriptions incompletely explain material risks and limitations
assessment: CONFIRMED LIVE partial coverage; not a claim that contraindications are absent everywhere.
quoted_text: TMT safety answer: "It is a standard, widely used test." ECG: "you will feel nothing more than the sticky pads." Echo: "is safe, including in pregnancy". Body composition: "estimate fat, muscle and water". Laboratory lists "fasting and post-meal blood sugar, HbA1c" and other tests without sampling-risk discussion.
why_it_breaches: These existing descriptions give benefits, preparation and some limitations but do not consistently describe relevant adverse effects and variable accuracy; a general footer disclaimer does not fill these procedure-level M3 gaps.
compliant_alternative: Add doctor-approved, procedure-specific text where each test is described: TMT: "Exercise testing can cause chest discomfort, abnormal heart rhythms or blood-pressure changes; rarely a serious cardiac event can occur. Suitability is assessed beforehand. False-positive and false-negative results are possible, and a normal result does not exclude all heart disease." ECG: "A resting ECG records electrical activity; it does not deliver electricity. Sticky pads may occasionally irritate the skin. It is a short recording and can miss intermittent or other heart problems; findings need clinical interpretation." Transthoracic Echo: "This scan uses ultrasound, not ionising radiation. Probe pressure can be uncomfortable. Image quality varies, and an Echo cannot directly exclude coronary artery narrowing or every heart condition; further assessment may be needed." Body composition: "Bioimpedance estimates are affected by hydration, meals, recent exercise and the device used. Results are not an exact measurement of every fat deposit and should be interpreted with strength tests and clinical assessment. Tell staff about pregnancy or implanted electronic devices before testing." Lab/home collection: "Blood collection may cause brief discomfort, bruising or light-headedness; infection is uncommon. Fasting is needed only for specified tests. Results vary with preparation, timing and other factors and must be interpreted with your history." Heart-care/check-up summaries: "Tests are chosen after assessment. Each has limitations and possible adverse effects, which your clinician will explain. Normal screening cannot exclude every condition or guarantee that a future heart event will not occur." Keep and link the existing detailed test descriptions; do not replace specific risk text with a generic guarantee disclaimer.
seo_aeo_note: Preserve preparation, timing, indications and existing FAQ URLs; concise risk/accuracy explanations improve answer quality without inventing success percentages.
client_input_needed: Dr. Ajay's confirmation of the procedures actually used, adverse-effect wording, contraindications and clinical escalation process.

title: Several treatment descriptions omit treatment-specific cautions or variable response
assessment: CONFIRMED LIVE gaps on listed pages; existing hypoglycaemia education and weight-medicine contraindications are preserved.
quoted_text: Thyroid: "Most are easily diagnosed with a blood test and well controlled with treatment." Hypertension: "medicines when needed". Pregnancy: "Insulin does not harm the baby." Teen counselling: "Most teenagers improve with counselling and family support." Programme: "12 consultations" and "4 HbA1c tests" list activity, not individual outcomes.
why_it_breaches: Under M3, these existing treatment descriptions need proportionate treatment-specific cautions and an explanation that response varies, rather than relying on disease-risk descriptions, session counts or the global disclaimer.
compliant_alternative: Add or replace the relevant passages with doctor-approved text: Thyroid: "Treatment depends on the cause. Response and monitoring needs vary. Too much or too little thyroid medicine can cause symptoms and complications; take it as prescribed and do not adjust the dose without advice." Hypertension: "Targets and response vary. Blood-pressure medicines can cause dizziness or other adverse effects, and some require kidney-function or electrolyte checks. Report problems rather than stopping treatment yourself." Pregnancy: replace the unqualified insulin sentence with "Insulin is commonly used when needed in pregnancy, but it can cause low blood sugar in the mother and requires individual dosing and monitoring. Treatment reduces risk but cannot guarantee a particular pregnancy outcome; your diabetes and obstetric teams coordinate care." Obesity/weight-medicine pages: "Weight change and health benefits vary, and weight may return after treatment changes. Medicines have contraindications and adverse effects, including the risks described here; no amount or timetable of weight loss is guaranteed." Nutrition: "Response varies with health, medicines and routine. Significant changes in food, activity or fasting may require medicine adjustments, particularly to avoid low blood sugar; agree changes with your clinician." Teen counselling: replace "Most teenagers improve..." with "Counselling and family support may help, but response and duration vary. Discussing difficult experiences can feel upsetting, and some young people need psychiatric assessment or other treatment. The care plan is reviewed if symptoms persist or worsen; this clinic is not an emergency service." Psychological assessment: "Scores can be affected by language, fatigue, anxiety and testing conditions. Testing may feel tiring or upsetting and cannot, by itself, determine every diagnosis or guarantee an educational outcome; findings are interpreted in context." Programme: "The programme organises follow-up; it does not guarantee glucose control or prevent every complication. Your plan and test frequency may change with clinical need. Medicines and tests have their own risks and limitations, which will be discussed before use." Keep the existing valid contraindications, low-sugar guidance and referral information rather than replacing them.
seo_aeo_note: Retain condition and therapy coverage, clinician attribution and useful FAQs; balanced, specific limitations preserve educational value without promotional certainty.
client_input_needed: Both doctors' clinical sign-off, actual treatment scope and approved monitoring/referral wording. Confirm programme scheduling can change as clinical need requires.
